newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable in slow late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable in slow late trading.

text.p: Indonesia's rupiah was stable against the dollar in slow late trading on Wednesday on the back of adequate money market liquidity, dealers said.
One Japanese bank dealer said long-term swap rates remained generally stable in slow trading while some local buying of spot rupiah was seen ahead of tax payments on Friday.

"The swap rates remain generally stable. There was some local rupiah buying ahead of tax payments on Friday, but they failed to boost sentiment on the local currency," another foreign bank dealer said.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,351.75/52.20 in late trading against an opening of 2,351.50/52.0.
Tomorrow and today rupiah were quoted at 2,351.25/51.65 and 2,351.0/51.30, respectively.
Dealers said they expected the central bank to raise its fixing rate on Thursday following increases on Monday and Tuesday. It did not increase the fixing rate today.
The central bank has maintained a three-to-four-point rupiah depreciation a week since late September.
"The rupiah is likely to move in a narrow range in trading on Thursday, with spot rupiah seen between 2,351.50/52.50," the Japanese bank dealer said.
Overnight swap was at 0.50/0.60 and tom/next at 0.43/0.48.
One-month swaps was at 15.00/15.50, two at 29.50/31.00, three at 42.75/43.75 and six at 87.00/87.50 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,350/2,542 and the conversion band to 2,350/2,398.
